title: Detect Repeated Characters in a Password Window
real_world_story: A security system analyzes passwords and authentication strings to detect suspicious repetition. It checks whether any fixed-size section of a password contains a repeated character.

real_world_connection.target_represents: Whether a repeated character exists inside any window of a specified size
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A sliding window that maintains character frequencies while moving across the string

problem_statement: Given a string and an integer K, determine whether any substring of length K contains a repeated character. Print YES if such a window exists; otherwise print NO.
task: Check every continuous window of K characters and determine whether at least one window contains a repeated character.
input_format: The first line contains a string S. The second line contains an integer K.
output_format: Print YES if any window of length K contains a repeated character. Otherwise, print NO.
constraints: S contains only English letters and digits

examples.explanation: The window 'aDde' contains the character 'd' twice.
Every window of length 3 contains unique characters.

expected_algorithm.name: Sliding Window
expected_algorithm.reason: A sliding window can maintain character frequencies efficiently while moving across the password.

hint: Create a window containing the first K characters.
Track the frequency of characters inside the window.
Move the window one character at a time.
Remove the character leaving the window and add the new character.
real_world_takeaway: Sliding Window techniques can efficiently inspect local sections of authentication strings for repeated or suspicious character patterns.
